subject: Cloud Computing
title: Spot Instances: Bargain Computing
description: A quick win: understand Spot Instances: Bargain Computing.

hook.text: Cloud providers have spare servers sitting idle. They sell them at a steep discount — with a catch.

buildup.text: Spot instances cost up to 90% less than regular pricing. The trade-off: they can vanish any time.

discovery.text: When demand rises, the provider reclaims spot capacity. Your workload gets a two-minute warning.

twist.text: Companies save millions using spot instances for batch jobs, rendering, and testing — interruptible work.

climax.text: Spot pricing turns idle servers into revenue. It's the cloud's version of standby airline tickets.

punchline.text: Cheap cloud exists. You just can't count on it staying.

quiz.question: What is the key trade-off of using spot instances?
options: They are much cheaper but can be terminated by the provider at any time
They are free but limited to 10 minutes of runtime
They run faster but cannot access the internet

details.summary: Spot instances provide spare cloud capacity at discounts of up to 90% compared to on-demand pricing. The trade-off is that the provider can reclaim them with short notice when capacity is needed. They are ideal for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads like batch processing and testing.
details.whyItMatters: Spot instances dramatically reduce costs for workloads that can tolerate interruption. Understanding when and how to use them can cut computing bills by more than half.
takeaways: Spot instances offer up to 90% discount on on-demand prices
They can be reclaimed by the provider with minutes of notice
Batch processing and CI/CD pipelines are ideal spot use cases

faq.question: When will a spot instance be interrupted?
faq.answer: Spot instances are reclaimed when the provider needs the capacity back for on-demand or reserved customers. AWS gives a two-minute warning. Google Cloud gives a 30-second warning for preemptible VMs. Interruption frequency varies by instance type, region, and time.

faq.question: How do you design for spot instance interruptions?
faq.answer: Save progress frequently through checkpointing. Distribute work across many small instances rather than few large ones. Mix spot and on-demand instances for baseline reliability. Use instance diversification across types and AZs to reduce simultaneous interruption risk.
